title: Interruption Mode Decision Lab and Rollout Gate
summary: Working session to define interruption/fallback modes for inference during capacity stress and rollout gating criteria. Decided on three interruption tiers (graceful degrade, degraded-async, emergency-cutover), test matrix, and owners for pilot. Agreed to run 2-week chaos window and produce a smoke-runbook for oncall.
topics: Latency vs cost vs quality tradeoffs
SRE test matrix and chaos plan

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-05
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~1h32m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Rourke, Priya Desai, Carlos Vega, Anika Rao; Eve Park, Noah Kim, Jasmine Li

[00:00] Maya Chen: okay, hi everyone, thanks for coming, um we'll try to keep this to an hour and a half ish — goal is to lock on interruption mode taxonomy and what the rollout gate looks like.
[00:22] Liam O'Rourke: yeah, thanks. quick note — I pushed the initial doc to the drive, it's called "interrupt-mode-primer". there's a diagram that shows three states. but it's rough.
[01:05] Eve Park: that helps, and just to be explicit from platform side, we need the behavior to be predictable for clients — spikes can't cause silent failures.
[01:30] Priya Desai: predictable meaning clear SLOs per mode? like latency SLO is relaxed to X in graceful-degrade, and in emergency-cutover traffic is throttled?
[01:48] Maya Chen: exactly, so we're thinking of defining: graceful-degrade (prefetch+partial responses), degraded-async (respond quickly with placeholder and async completion), and emergency-cutover (stop serving on this pool, route to alternate).
[02:10] Noah Kim: quick Q: are we assuming KV cache is preserved in degraded-async? because that changes latency profile.
[02:26] Carlos Vega: good spot, KV cache will be partially preserved in graceful-degrade; degraded-async will evict some long-tail shards to free memory. we need metrics for eviction rate and miss-stall time.
[02:40] Jasmine Li: for product, can you restate user-visible effects? are we returning partial text, or pre-baked generic message?
[02:55] Liam O'Rourke: partial text for graceful-degrade — we stream what we can, maybe lower max tokens; degraded-async returns a 202 with a token to poll or a webhook; emergency-cutover returns a friendly 503 and routes to fallback model/version.
[03:25] Maya Chen: that implies API change for degraded-async; ops needs to own polling contract.
[03:45] Priya Desai: yeah, I noted that; also need to lock on idempotency keys and webhook retry semantics. we'll draft patterns.
[04:10] Anika Rao: how does this impact pricing or billing signals? customers will be confused if responses are async.
[04:25] Maya Chen: for pilot we don't change billing, but we will label responses and include a header so PMs can display correct UX.
[04:40] Liam O'Rourke: tradeoffs: graceful-degrade keeps latency best but costs more per token; degraded-async saves GPU cycles but adds implementation complexity; emergency-cutover is cheapest but worst UX. we should map each client class to allowed modes.
[05:10] Eve Park: rounding back to rollout gate — we need an objective threshold. I propose: failover should only auto-run if error rate > 2% sustained for 3 minutes AND regional capacity exhaustion > 70%. thoughts?
[05:35] Carlos Vega: number seems OK but we need a composite signal: CPU saturation, NVMM pressure, in-flight requests, and queue latency 95p. can combine into a 4-flag check.
[05:55] Maya Chen: yes, gate = (error-rate + capacity) + infra flags. also canary must be clean: canary traffic must show <1% error and 10% lower latency deviation.
[06:20] Noah Kim: let's be careful with the canary numbers — 10% is tight on some heavy embeddings routes. maybe route-specific thresholds.
[06:40] Priya Desai: agree, we'll make threshold per-route and per-model. I'll include the route-level thresholds in the test matrix.
[07:00] Jasmine Li: timeline? When are we aiming to pilot this?
[07:08] Maya Chen: proposed pilot: two-week window starting 2027-04-25, small cohort of internal customers, then open beta.
[07:20] Anika Rao: can ops and oncall handle extra noise? need to schedule rotation.
[07:30] Priya Desai: we can, but we need a smoke-runbook with clear triage steps — who flips what flags, where to look for KV eviction spikes, and which dashboards to pager. I'll own the runbook.
[07:50] Liam O'Rourke: technical detail — streaming partial responses requires us to manage KV cache context-length differently. we may need to cap prefix caching for graceful-degrade to avoid huge memory growth.
[08:12] Carlos Vega: that's where I want telemetry: prefix-cache-size-by-epoch, eviction-latency, and net-memory-footprint. if we don't have those, it's blind.
[08:35] Maya Chen: action: Carlos add three metrics; Priya will add test matrix; Liam will diagram flows.
[08:50] Eve Park: can we also add a user-visible manifest for PMs that says exactly what UX to expect so they can change product copy?
[09:05] Jasmine Li: yes I'll draft the manifest if you give me the list of modality changes.
[09:18] Anika Rao: ok pragmatic question — what about dedicated vs hosted? some dedicated customers may not want emergency-cutover to route to hosted.
[09:35] Liam O'Rourke: we need a policy table by customer tier: hosted can fallback to other regions or model variants; dedicated must have a private fallback behavior (i.e., degrade in-place) unless they opt into cross-tenant fallback which they usually don't.
[09:56] Noah Kim: that means for dedicated customers we need finer-grain controls and probably a separate rollout gate. makes pilot planning trickier.
[10:12] Maya Chen: let's scope the initial pilot to hosted and internal dedicated testbeds only — don't go GA with enterprise until we have 6 weeks of stability.
[10:30] Priya Desai: got it. For the SRE test matrix, do we include KV eviction, kernel fallback, and batch-split scenarios?
[10:45] Liam O'Rourke: yes include kernel fallback (GPU->CPU fallback), long-sequence eviction, and bursty small-requests. also test quantization skew on some models.
[11:05] Carlos Vega: note on telemetry: some of these metrics require a minor agent bump to the serving side to expose per-request eviction tag. I'll open a PR.
[11:20] Maya Chen: good. Any open objections to the three-mode taxonomy?
[11:28] Eve Park: none from me.
[11:32] Jasmine Li: no.
[11:35] Noah Kim: no.
[11:38] Priya Desai: I think we should add a graceful rollback plan for canary that includes automatic revert if model quality drop > 5% on eval set.
[11:50] Liam O'Rourke: yea, and tie that to our eval pipeline — run spot evals on the canary traffic.
[12:05] Maya Chen: next steps recap: diagrams (Liam), SRE matrix + runbook (Priya), metrics (Carlos), gate doc + leader share (Maya), pilot schedule (Anika). We'll reconvene April 19 for demo of artifacts.
[12:35] Anika Rao: I'll set calendar and invite oncall leads.
[12:42] Maya Chen: anything else?
[12:50] Carlos Vega: small ask — add a column in the runbook for who to call in sequence; during chaos we need a single leader.
[12:59] Priya Desai: noted.
[13:05] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript had wrong attribution a few times; removed long silences. There were a couple of crosstalk moments at ~09:30 and ~11:40 where speakers overlapped.
